encounter_rewrites.title: Act I: Pitgaveny
encounter_rewrites.body: This is the moment the chronicles remember as the hinge between legal kingship and actual power. Duncan's army is broken, the court hesitates, and Macbeth steps into a vacancy that no speech can repair. The throne waits for him not because it is right, but because he arrives first to claim it. In this vacuum of authority, might replaces law entirely. The old order fractures under the weight of his arrival, leaving only the immediate reality of who holds the sword.
reaction_rewrites: The crown now belongs to whoever can occupy it, and Macbeth proves he can move faster than the surviving royal party. The next claim will remember it. In Alba, the record outlives the moment.
Duncan's death ends the argument for one claimant and begins the harder argument over legitimacy. The court will count the cost later. In Alba, the record outlives the moment.

encounter_rewrites.title: Act II: Crinan's Rising
encounter_rewrites.body: The uprising is personal, dynastic, and short-lived. It proves that the old king's family still has political reach, yet lacks the raw force to dislodge Macbeth once the new regime has fully hardened around him. Crinan's attempt to reclaim his father's legacy fails against the momentum of a crown secured by violence. The court remembers this not as a victory for the rebels, but as a warning that bloodlines cannot always override the reality of power.
reaction_rewrites: The rebellion dies fast enough to remind the court that Macbeth is not merely holding the throne; he is willing to defend it. The next claim will remember it. In Alba, the record outlives the moment.
Crinan's death turns private grievance into dynastic warning. The court will count the cost later. In Alba, the record outlives the moment.

encounter_rewrites.title: Act III: Lulach Crowned at Scone
encounter_rewrites.body: The coronation is brief, fragile, and astonishingly important for the history of Alba. It proves that the kingdom has not simply fallen into Malcolm's hands; it still contains another claim, another memory, and another attempt to keep the Moray line alive against the tide of usurpation. Lulach stands as a temporary shield, buying time for the old house to assert its existence in a world increasingly dominated by new bloodlines.
reaction_rewrites: Lulach's crown gives the defeated line one last public form. The next claim will remember it. In Alba, the record outlives the moment.
The ceremony matters precisely because it is the first of its kind in the record. The court will count the cost later. In Alba, the record outlives the moment.
